options.what: Once a piece of work builds clean and the tests pass, it goes to the shared copy without asking you. You stop being interrupted for it.
options.costs: Nothing of your time. Work reaches the shared copy before you have looked at it, so if you dislike something you are reverting it there instead of catching it here.

question: An animated background band is stored in a slot whose size was fixed back when no act had one, and a real band needs about four thousand times that. Fixing the slot is easy; the question is how big to make it. A band's size depends entirely on how big an author draws it, and the legal range runs from 302 bytes to about 112 KB - a 380x spread. Whatever we pick, an author who draws a bigger band than that gets a build failure, so this is really a question about how much background animation you want to be possible without an engine change.

options.name: Pick a generous ceiling now and refuse politely above it
options.what: We reserve room for a band up to 16 tiles wide by 8 tall - about eight times the one Aurora just drew, and comfortably inside the spare room that already exists next to it. Anything bigger stops the build with a message naming the limit, instead of the cryptic collision we get today. Authors never think about this again until they hit the ceiling.
options.costs: About 32 KB of cartridge space set aside whether or not an act uses it. You have roughly 350 KB spare, so it is not tight. If you ever want a band bigger than that, raising it is a small change but it is a change.

options.name: Reserve enough for the biggest band that could ever exist
options.what: Room for a band covering every tile the background has. No author can ever hit a limit, and this question never comes back.
options.costs: About 112 KB set aside permanently, which is very nearly all the spare room in that part of the cartridge. It would leave that neighbourhood with almost nothing left for anything else later.

options.name: Re-measure the layout every time the band changes size
options.what: No space is wasted and no ceiling exists. The layout is recomputed to fit whatever the author actually drew.
options.costs: Every time you resize a band, the cartridge layout has to be re-measured and re-approved in the assembler's repo - a deliberate act in a different project. It turns a normal art tweak into a cross-project chore, which cuts against the whole point of the effects work: that something you build in the editor just reaches the game.

recommend.because: It is the only option that costs you nothing at authoring time and does not spend the room you may want later. It also matches how this engine already handles the same kind of limit elsewhere - the number of bands is a declared ceiling with a guard that names it - so it is the consistent choice rather than a new idea. And the failure it produces is a sentence telling an author their band is too big, which is the failure you want if you are ever going to hit one.

detail: ojz_bg_anim's frozen allotment is 2 bytes (measured from the disabled stub: BgAnim_Table u16 = 0 plus Data.empty). Section size derives exactly as 46 + cols*rows*8*32 (2 + 12 + 32 header/record/pointer bytes + cols*rows*BANKS*32 bank blob); aurora's authored 8x4 band = 8238, matching the observed span [0x3B270,0x3D29E) exactly. Range over legal author geometries: 1x1=302, 8x4=8238, 16x8=32814, 32x14 (all 448 tiles)=114734. Slack before the hardware-pinned dac_banks anchor at 0x48000 is ~119 KB. Mechanism: native.rs:2947-2970 makes a section an anchor (Pinned) when its frozen true base exceeds the running chain end, so growth collides with the next pinned chain rather than flowing. Precedent for the ceiling shape: BGANIM_MAX_BANDS, a declared ceiling with a span guard (tools/test_bg_emit.py::TestBgAnimBandCeiling). Raised independently by the aurora lane (from band arithmetic) and this lane (from sigil's placement mechanism) - different enumeration parameters, so corroboration rather than echo.

Reserving room for the biggest background animation that could ever exist turns out to cost nothing at all, because the space it would use is already an unused gap sitting in the middle of the cartridge, doing nothing, and it cannot be used by anything else. So the choice is really just: take the free room, or don't.

options.what: Every background animation an author could ever draw fits. No limit, no build failures, and this question never comes back. It fits with about 4 KB to spare.

detail: SUPERSEDES d-6. Two corrections from aurora, both verified firsthand here. (1) Per-band ceiling was the wrong unit: BgAnim_Banks is one blob for ALL bands in the act, so history's 32x4 + 16x4 both pass a 16x8 per-band ceiling while their sum (192 slots = 49,152 B) overflows a 32 KB allotment. (2) The historical content is real, not hypothetical: b0e5a661's editor_bg_override.json carries 32x4 + 16x4 / 8 phases = 192 slots, and games/sonic4/data/generated/ojz/act1/bg_anim_banks.bin is 49,152 bytes on disk right now (stale artifact the stub path never rewrote) - two independent sources, no shared step. Worst case is provably bounded: bands pack contiguously from slot 0 as a prefix of tiles (validate_band_coherence), so total slots <= BG_TILE_CAPACITY = 448 regardless of band count; max section = 2 + 44*BGANIM_MAX_BANDS(4) + 448*8*32 = 114,866. Slack check re-derived here rather than taken from the booking, because the booking's '~119 KB' subtracted only HeightMaps: the five shifting labels (Map_TestObj, Ani_Sonic, Ani_Tails, Ani_Particle, HeightMaps+Rot) pack into [0x27E72,0x2AEE0) and the free hole is AFTER them, [0x2AEE0,0x48000) = 119,072 B. Worst-case section from 0x27E70 plus the 12,398 B of shifted labels ends at 0x46F50, clearing the hardware-pinned dac_banks anchor at 0x48000 by 4,272 B. Interior hole = no ROM growth. Aurora's stated realistic bar was 49,152 ('can restore what was lost'); worst case dominates it at no cost. Note BG_BAND_RESERVE = 128 tiles / BG_STATIC_TILE_BUDGET = 320 is a separate authoring-side budget and is NOT this number.

detail: RETRACTS the central premise of d-7 AND of the DEFERRED_WORK booking. All three of us (this lane, aurora, and the booking itself) read the [HeightMaps+0x2000, Dac_Temp_Blip) gap in the frozen boundary table as ~119,072 B of slack. It is not slack: s4.debug.lst lines 2225-2229 show AngleTable 0x2AEE0, SolidityTable 0x2AFE0, Map_Sonic 0x2B0E0, DPLC_Sonic 0x2CD60, Art_Sonic 0x2D6A0 filling it. Measured on the ROM: only 43.8% of that span is zero. THE BOOKING WARNED AGAINST THIS EXACT INFERENCE ('the golden table records BASES ONLY - a gap is an ALLOTMENT, never proven free space') and then committed it two paragraphs later on a different label pair; the frozen table is a BOUNDARY table listing a subset of labels, so gaps in it are invisible content, and only the .lst or the ROM can tell you which. Corrected free space, by constant-byte run scan of s4.debug.bin: the only real hole before the anchor is 0x4535D-0x48000 = 11,427 B (caveat: I have NOT established whether that tail is unowned or is trailing blank tiles belonging to Art_Sonic, so treat 11,427 as an upper bound and shape-specific - the plain shape will differ and the ceiling must be the MINIMUM across shapes). Against that: aurora's 8x4 band = 8,238 fits with ~3.2 KB spare; history's 32x4+16x4 = 49,242 does not; the provable worst case 114,866 is not close. Other holes found: 0x48B40-0x50000 = 29,888 (inside the DAC bank window, hardware-aligned, presumed unusable) and 0xAEC2-0x10000 = 20,798 (before the object code bank). Art_Sonic is ~97,469 B, consistent with this engine's uncompressed sprite art. EndOfRom 0xa3290 = 668,304 against a 715,010-byte debug file, so 'space after the end' means GROWING the ROM, not filling a hole - d-7's 'no ROM growth' claim does not survive either.

detail: THE PREMISE OF d-9/d-10 WAS WRONG AND THIS IS THE THIRD CORRECTION ON THIS QUESTION - but unlike the first two it came from measurement, not from me re-reading a table. Verified firsthand at sigil native.rs:2325: the measuring pass spreads provisional pins by `*p += 0x400 * rank`, and ojz_bg_anim is rank-adjacent to test_mappings, so a growing section gets exactly one 0x400 step. Room = frozen allotment + 1024 = 1038 (s4) / 1026 (s4.debug), matching sigil's own reported spans 0x40E/0x402 and an 814-builds/1070-fails bisection in both shapes. No escape: derive_frozen_table routes through the same measure_or_spread so grow-then-refreeze fails identically, and repin needs listings that need a successful build. ROM room is genuinely 11,424 B (corrected from d-9's 11,427; the run scan had started 3 bytes inside Art_Sonic's own trailing zeros) - that number was right and simply is not the binding one. WHAT LANDED ANYWAY at ef3cc47b: an authoring-time refusal naming geometry, size with arithmetic, ceiling, overage, which limit bound it, and how many slots fit, totalling all bands rather than per band; plus tools/bganim_room.py, wired into build.sh, which derives both limits every sonic4 build and FAILS LOUDLY rather than reporting a number it could not measure (the agent's own poison found that hole in it and fixed it). Byte-neutral, four shapes, CRCs unchanged with freshness proven, pytest 1347->1361 zero failures. Named ask sent to the sigil lane with the line, the derivation, the bisection and an explicit statement that we are not proposing their design. Also flagged, untouched, one line to fix and your call: games/sonic4/data/generated/ojz/act1/bg_anim_banks.bin is a committed 49,152-byte stale artifact the stub arm never rewrites.

detail: SUPERSEDES d-11. The sigil lane read my named ask and corrected my sort: I filed it as genuinely-new work and it is not. native.rs:2368 `image_lens_pinned` already computes `force_scratch = fixture && !is_phase_bank && is_position_independent(s)`, measuring a qualifying section at a disjoint scratch slot instead of its frozen pin - and its comment at :2357-2365 states our exact problem and its exact solution verbatim. I read around :2325 without reading :2357-2365, which is this suite's own bar about reading the lines surrounding a citation, missed in the message where I was careful about everything else. question: Your recorded regression net for the level - 1,721 ticks of played-back input that the game re-checks against a stored fingerprint - stops matching partway through, because Sonic's new insta-shield deliberately changes what an airborne jump press does. The mismatch is the new feature working, not a fault. Re-recording the net is the fix, but re-recording also silently swallows any OTHER change that crept into the same run, and swallowing those is exactly what the net exists to prevent. So: re-record now, prove first, or leave it.

options.name: Prove the shield is the only change, then re-record
options.what: I build a throwaway copy of the game with the insta-shield taken back out and play the same recording through it. If it matches all the way to the end, the shield is provably the only thing that moved, and the re-record absorbs nothing else. Then I re-record and you get your full net back with that proof in the commit.
options.costs: Half a day rather than an hour, and I have not yet confirmed the shield comes back out cleanly - if it does not, this falls back to one of the other two and you have spent the time for nothing.

options.name: Just re-record it
options.what: The net is live again today, covering the whole run including the new move.
options.costs: If anything else drifted in the same stretch of play, it becomes the new normal and nobody ever finds out. That is the one failure this net was built to catch.

options.name: Leave it alone for now
options.what: Nothing is spent. The second recorded net, the slide one, is unaffected and still watching - it has no jump presses to disturb.
options.costs: The bigger net stays dark, so a real regression in that stretch of play goes unnoticed until you rule on this, and every later change makes proving the shield was the only cause harder.

recommend.because: The net's whole value is that nobody re-records it casually, so the one thing worth buying here is the proof that this re-record is honest - and it is cheap and available right now, while the shield is the only change since the last good stamp. Every week that passes makes that proof impossible, which turns option one into option two by default. If the take-it-back-out step turns out messy I will stop and tell you rather than quietly re-recording anyway.
